anomalies.observed: The netlist leaves every VDD pin on both MCUs unconnected; FCC1's VDDA and NAVC1's VDDA/VSSA are also not connected to supply or ground nets. The +3.3V and +3V3 rails do not connect to those MCU supply pins.
anomalies.expected: Both MCUs must have their VDD pins powered from the 3.3 V rail, with their analog supply and ground pins connected appropriately. The specification says 3.3 V feeds both MCUs.

evidence.quote: 3.3V feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Neither MCU can operate without its supply pins powered; the board will not function as the specified flight controller.

anomalies.observed: The UART3 connector TX and RX nets are connected directly to FCC1 pins 48 and 73, respectively; the MCU library identifies both pins as VCAP.
anomalies.expected: UART signals should use MCU UART-capable signal pins. VCAP pins are internal-regulator outputs and should be connected to their required decoupling capacitors, not routed to an external UART connector.
anomalies.impact: The UART3 interface cannot work as intended, and external loading or signaling on the connector may disrupt or damage the MCU's internal core supply.

anomalies.observed: FCC HSE nets connect to pins PE6 and PE7 rather than its PH0/PH1 oscillator pins. NAVC HSE nets do not connect to NAVC1; its PH0/PH1 pins instead connect to C37/C38.
anomalies.expected: The 25 MHz external crystals should connect to the HSE oscillator pins of their respective MCUs. The specification identifies an HSE crystal for both MCUs.
anomalies.impact: The MCU high-speed external clocks will not operate as intended, preventing or compromising normal MCU startup and clocking.
